correctness.rationale: Cube automorphisms send any length-k geodesic to a standard nested-prefix chain. Hamming distance to prefix j equals t-(2u_j-j); reflection of a ±1 walk gives exactly C(k,r)-C(k,r-1) words for each fixed t with r≤t≤k-r. Summing over k-2r+1 possible t and multiplying by (1+z)^(d-k) proves the identity. Its largest exponent gives exact eccentricity, and unordered Hamming-endpoint pairs times k! enumerates distinct geodesics. Finite checker directly compared all shells for d≤12 and all oriented rooted paths for d≤6 and optimal counts to d≤10. These tests do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Multiple actual semantic published-finding corpus queries, accessible same-week claim scan, relevant primary 2026 full-text comparison, and searches of equivalent Boolean-chain and hypercube-path domination formulations found no stronger or equivalent coverage of the all-geodesic distance-shell polynomial and optimal-path multiplicity. Primary hypercube domination articles from 2001 and 2003 remain abstract-only, a genuine priority risk; novelty is best-knowledge, not certified.
residual_risks: Two directly relevant older hypercube-path-domination articles (2001, 2003) were not inspected in full; an implicit all-shell or chain-distance result could alter priority.
The 2017 general shortest-path eccentricity paper was available only at abstract/bibliographic level.
Related terminology from coding theory and ballot paths may index an earlier exact distribution; searched several aliases without finding an equivalence, not an exhaustive proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The full distance-shell distribution, not just a radius, is a natural invariant of paths as facilities in a hypercube. The all-dimensional closed ballot polynomial determines coverage at every tolerance, while strict parity classification and exact counts describe all optimum shortest paths. The result answers a concrete instance of the recent ESP direction, with usable enumerative information beyond existence/complexity and independent conceptual content of Boolean reflection identities; no artificial finite slice is imposed.
